changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders at renewal or evaluation, open with their own numbers rather than our average: 'Here are your approvals by market, card type and issuer, the reasons behind the declines, the money left on the table, and what we would fix.' Use 'approvals', not 'authorization'. Use the average uplift only as supporting context after their own numbers.
changes.why: We pitched the average uplift and the buyer rejected it outright ('that's an average. What's mine?', 'I can't take an average to my CFO.'), and he talks about 'approvals' and 'Money left on the table', not authorization rates.

changes.change: Proof offer for any customer who questions performance or is weighing local acquiring: 'We'll run your approval analysis on your own traffic, by country, card type and issuer, with the reasons, and deliver it in days.' Confirm the turnaround the payments performance team can commit to before using a specific number of days.
changes.why: Adyen won with a country-level test on the customer's own traffic, and our equivalent market-by-market analysis held fixable findings but arrived three weeks after he asked, when the test was already finished.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with a payments leader: 'A named person at Stripe who looks at your approval rates by market every month, plus support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.'
changes.why: The buyer asked 'who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month' and the rep had no name, after nine to ten months without a review on an account counted healthy because it had 'no tickets', so reactive response times did not answer his concern.
